# S3 Control

Manage access points, account Block Public Access, Multi-Region Access Points and shared S3 bucket tags.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `s3control` |
| Signing name | `s3` |
| Wire protocol | REST XML |
| API version | `2018-08-20` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Access-point alias object I/O; persistent MRAP control-plane transitions |
| Selected operations | 24 of 97 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#s3-control) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Access point ARN and host-style s3-accesspoint endpoints; MRAP SigV4a/accesspoint.s3-global data plane; cross-account bucket attachment; VPC network-origin enforcement.
- Public ACLs remain unsupported by S3; IgnorePublicAcls and BlockPublicAcls are stored configuration. RestrictPublicBuckets blocks public-policy access outside the owner account, without AWS service-principal exemptions.
- Public-policy status reuses the existing S3 unconditional-wildcard analysis rather than the complete AWS trust inference algorithm.
- Batch Operations jobs, Storage Lens, Access Grants, Object Lambda, Outposts, directory buckets and FSx access points remain outside the profile.
- MRAP tagging is unsupported by the modeled tagging API; MRAPs appear in inventory without tags.
- Only commercial AWS general purpose buckets and ARNs are supported; SDK IP-address endpoints cannot resolve account host prefixes.
- Checksum-required MRAP requests validate Content-MD5 when supplied; missing checksum headers and alternate flexible checksum algorithms are not enforced.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
